notes:
Structure: three long horizontal runs (top rail y~140->170, middle rail
y~230->262, and two separate short bottom runs) crossed by six vertical columns
at x~55 (sources), 152, 239, 319, 402 and 458 (resistor). Four two-terminal
parts sit IN SERIES inside the horizontal runs and therefore split them:
Inductor 0 and Capacitor 4 are in the top rail, Capacitor 6 and Inductor 15 are
in the middle rail, Capacitor 14 is in the bottom-left run. Every column/rail
intersection was checked on the raw pixel grid: they are all plain thickened
4-way or T junctions - there is not a single semicircular hop anywhere in this
drawing, so no crossing is a break.

Net map:
0  = middle-rail LEFT segment plus the resistor return. GND 5 (drawn sideways at
     the far left, three vertical bars, lead exiting right at y~229) runs right
     to the filled junction at (49,230) on the source column, on to the junction
     at (151,240) on the Zener1/Diode7 column, and ends on the left plate of
     Capacitor 6 at x~189. GND 16 sits under Resistor 17, so the resistor's
     bottom lead is the same reference net. Terminals: GND 5, GND 16,
     V-DC 3 bottom, I-DC 8 top, Zener 1 bottom, Diode 7 top, Capacitor 6 left
     plate, Resistor 17 bottom (8 terminals).
n1 = top rail LEFT stub: corner at (55,139) down to the top of V-DC 3, and right
     to the left lead of Inductor 0 at x~85. Two terminals.
n2 = top rail MIDDLE segment: right lead of Inductor 0 (x~123) -> T at (160,150)
     down to Zener 1 -> T at (241,158) down to Diode 2 -> left plate of
     Capacitor 4 at x~279.
n3 = top rail RIGHT segment: right plate of Capacitor 4 (x~285) -> T at (323,163)
     down to Zener 11 -> corner at (402,167) down to Diode 12.
n4 = middle rail MIDDLE segment: right plate of Capacitor 6 (x~194) -> junction
     at (238,247) (Diode 2 above, Zener 9 below) -> junction at (319,253)
     (Zener 11 above, Diode 10 below) -> left lead of Inductor 15 at x~352.
     Six terminals, the biggest signal node.
n5 = middle rail RIGHT segment: right lead of Inductor 15 (x~383) -> junction at
     (403,260) (Diode 12 above, Diode 13 below) -> corner at (459,262) -> down
     to the top of Resistor 17.
n6 = bottom-left run, LEFT of Capacitor 14: bottom of I-DC 8 down x~41 to the
     corner at (41,330), right to the left plate of Capacitor 14 at x~76. Two
     terminals, nothing else on the run (verified pixel by pixel).
n7 = bottom-left run, RIGHT of Capacitor 14: right plate (x~82) -> T at (139,335)
     up to Diode 7 -> corner/end at (229,338) up to Zener 9. The run stops dead
     at x=229; the band x=230..307 is completely blank.
n8 = bottom-right run: corner at (310,336) up to Diode 10, right to the corner at
     (400,339), up to Diode 13. Two terminals. This run is physically separate
     from the bottom-left run (78 px of blank paper between them), so n7 and n8
     are different nets.

Judgment calls:
(a) Both GND symbols get net "0" per the rule that all grounds in one drawing
     are one reference, even though GND 5 (far left, middle rail) and GND 16
     (bottom right, under the resistor) are drawn far apart with no wire between
     them. This is the only place where two ink-separate runs are merged.
(b) The four series parts inside the rails are the whole story of this circuit
     and are easy to miss: Inductor 0 and Capacitor 4 break the top rail into
     n1/n2/n3, Capacitor 6 and Inductor 15 break the middle rail into 0/n4/n5,
     Capacitor 14 breaks the bottom-left run into n6/n7. Each was confirmed at
     the pixel level (both plates/the coil sit across the rail, with the rail
     ink stopping at one plate and restarting at the other).
(c) No hops anywhere. Every column terminates on the rail it meets (a T) or
     passes through it with a thickened 4-way blob; the columns at x=152, 239,
     319 and 402 each carry a device above AND below the middle rail, so those
     are genuine 4-way nodes, not crossings. The junctions at (49,230),
     (151,240), (238,247), (319,253) and (403,260) all show the vertical and the
     horizontal continuous with 2-4 px of extra ink at the meeting point.
(d) Terminal order for every 2-terminal part is upper-then-lower for the
     vertical ones and left-then-right for the horizontal ones, as drawn. Per
     the protocol this does not affect any metric, so I did not rely on reading
     the diode/zener polarity marks (for the record Zener 1 and Zener 11 are
     drawn cathode-bar-up, Zener 9 cathode-bar-up, Diode 2/7/10/12/13 all have
     the bar toward the bottom of the symbol).
(e) Tier-2 simcheck finding, kept deliberately: net n6 has NO DC PATH TO GROUND.
     It joins only the bottom terminal of I-DC 8 to the left plate of Capacitor
     14, and both a current source and a capacitor are open at DC. The ink is
     unambiguous - the wire leaves the bottom of the 1A source, turns right at
     (41,330) and dead-ends on the capacitor plate at x=76 with nothing else
     touching it over that whole run - so this is a real property of the drawing,
     not a mis-trace. No Tier 1 fault: no source is shorted, there is no
     disconnected island, no net touches fewer than two terminals, the current
     source has a return path through the capacitor, and no loop of voltage
     sources/inductors exists (V-DC 3 and Inductor 0 are in series between "0"
     and n2, not in parallel).
